newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila share index ends down in heavy volume.
newsitem.headline: Manila share index ends down in heavy volume.

text.p: * Five thirdliner issues frozen in late trade
The Manila stocks index ended in negative territory on Monday as thirdlliners continued to grab the spotlight from blue chips, traders said.

"Everyone's concentration is on the speculatives and unless people are saturated with these increases, we won't see the index inching up substantially," Jose Ricardo Garcia, Diversified Securities executive vice-president said.
The index fell 9.43 points, or 0.28 percent, to 3,323.10.
Eight thirdliner issues were up by 40 percent and more in Monday's trade.

The Philippine Stock Exchange (PSE) had to freeze five tertiary issues in late trade. They were Imperial Resources Inc, Itogon Suyoc Mines Inc A and B, Marsteel Consolidated Inc A and B, Atok Big Wedge Co and Acoje Holdings Inc as they had reached the 50 percent ceiling put on price rises in a single session.

"Judging from the way the index is moving, this is a healthy pause and a prelude for the market before it tests the all-time high of 3,376 if not late this week then by next week," Nathan Lozada, assistant vice-president at Philippine Asia Equity said.

Most of the blue chips led by PLDT were down except for oil refiner Petron Corp which bucked the trend by closing up 25 centavos, or 2.38 percent, at 10.75 pesos due to the advancing of the date for full oil industry deregulation.

While the gloom on Wall Street dampened local sentiment as well, profit-taking on Ayala Corp and Benpres, winners of the Metropolitan Water and Sewerage System (MWSS) bidding, also pulled down the index early in the session.
Immediate support level of 3,300 may be tested on Tuesday, traders said. - KATHERINE ESPINA 63 2 841-8939 Fax 8176267
